 Prosecutors and defense attorneys are years apart on when the Turning Point USA founder's accused killer should face trial
 By
 Michael Ruiz , Adam Sabes Fox News 
 Published
 November 9, 2026 10:40am EST
 |

 close Video Judge sets June 2028 trial date for Charlie Kirk murder suspect 
 A judge has set a trial date for Tyler Robinson, the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk.
 NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!
 PROVO, Utah — The judge overseeing the case against accused assassin Tyler Robinson set a trial date on Monday for June 21, 2028, after prosecutors and defense attorneys sought dramatically different start times for the trial of the man accused of gunning down Charlie Kirk last year.
 Robinson, 22, is accused of assassinating the 31-year-old Kirk on Sept. 10, 2025, during a Turning Point USA event at Utah Valley University in Orem by shooting him with a .30-06 hunting rifle from a rooftop on the other side of the campus courtyard.
 Judge Tony Graf Jr. said Monday he reserved 105 days for the trial.
 TYLER ROBINSON HEARING ENDS WITHOUT TRIAL DATE SET, PROMPTING FIERY PLEA FROM ERIKA KIRK'S LAWYER 
 Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing conservative activist Charlie Kirk, is seen in court in his first in-person court appearance on Dec. 11, 2025. (Pool/KSL-TV) 
 "Today's decision to delay the trial of the man accused of murdering our beloved Charlie until at least June 2028, is deeply disappointing," Kirk's family said in a statement. "While nothing will restore the time we have lost with Charlie, every additional day without justice prolongs our family's pain and forces us to wait even longer for accountability."
 As the designated victim's representative under Utah law, widow Erika Kirk has a right to see a speedy resolution to the case. That does not outweigh Robinson's right to a fair trial, however.
 Responding to Erika Kirk's request for a trial by October 2027, Graf said that timeline would leave Robinson's defense too little time to prepare and pointed to other scheduling hurdles such as the holidays and previously scheduled trial obligations in other cases for attorneys on both sides.
 Graf said the June 2028 trial date leaves room for hearings after defense attorney Richard Novak's expected January federal trial in San Jose, California, gives both sides seven weeks after juror questionnaires are due May 3, 2028, and sets a firm date for lining up witnesses and experts.
 Defense attorney Richard Novak in 4th District Court in Provo on Tuesday, May 19, 2026 during a hearing for Tyler Robinson, accused in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune via Pool) 
 As Graf was discussing the victim representative's right to object to future attempts to delay the trial, Novak showed Robinson something written on a yellow notepad.
 The judge said a report from both the prosecution and defense is due by Dec. 14, requiring each party to "file an initial conflict and progress report addressing their ability to meet this order's deadlines."
 Jeffrey Neiman, lawyer for the Kirk family, said during the hearing that the June 2028 trial "does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family."
 "The Kirk family strongly asks the court that the schedule will not move unless something truly significant requires it to be moved. The family has waited long enough already. They should not have to wait any longer for this. And with that, we will let the process play out," Neiman said.
 Attorney Jeffrey Neiman, representing the Kirk family, is pictured in court during the Tyler Robinson case, who is charged in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk, in 4th District Court in Provo on Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026. (Francisco Kjolseth/The Salt Lake Tribune via Pool) 
 Utah County prosecutors asked in court documents and oral arguments for Jan. 31, 2028, as their preferred trial date but said they could be ready in October 2027. Robinson's defense team has proposed late 2029 as a "soft target" trial date.
 Staci Visser, one of Robinson's defense lawyers, said at a hearing in October that the state's timeline is "not practical" due to large amounts of discovery.
 "Discovery review is foundational," she said. "It impacts everything else."
 MICHAEL RUIZ: TYLER ROBINSON BLAMES TRUMP POST IN PUSH FOR CAMERA BAN 
 The court was also attempting to work with both sides to avoid setting a date that conflicts with previously scheduled trials they have in other cases.
 Charlie Kirk speaks at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images) 
 One directly conflicted with the prosecution's desired start date, a federal racketeering case Novak has scheduled for Jan. 10, 2028.
 "The reality is rushing to trial does not lead to closure. It does not lead to finality. It leads to mistakes," he said at a hearing on Oct. 23.
 CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION SUSPECT'S LAWYERS MIRROR NOTORIOUS KILLER'S TACTICAL DELAY STRATEGY: FMR PROSECUTOR 
 Both sides agreed that setting a trial earlier, which would be interrupted for a break during the holidays, could put potential jurors and witnesses in a bind.
 SEND US A TIP 
 The case's pace has even attracted criticism from President Donald Trump, who wrote on the Truth Social platform that the judge was doing "a terrible job" moving things along.
 UTAH PROSECUTORS ASK JUDGE TO SHUT DOWN DELAY TACTICS IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION CASE 
 A map of the UVU campus shows key locations surrounding the courtyard where Charlie Kirk was shot and killed on Sept. 10, 2025. (After-Action report for Utah Valley University) 
 "This case should be tried within a month, not three years — and it should be over with," Trump wrote. "The judge is desecrating the memory of the Great Charlie Kirk, while taking forever to ask questions that people already know the answer to. The whole Country is mocking him and our 'Legal' System. JUSTICE FOR CHARLIE!"
 Robinson's lawyers used the president's post to argue that news cameras should be kicked out of the courtroom. Graf denied the request, as he has done several times previously.
 Judge Tony Graf presides over Tyler Robinson’s preliminary hearing. (Pool) 
 "He's very slow — he's very deliberate on making decisions," Donna Rotunno, a criminal defense attorney and Fox News contributor, told "Fox & Friends" Monday. "I do hope he sets a trial date. The only reason he wouldn't is if he says there are too many motions that are still outstanding and we need to get through those first."

 "Justice delayed this long stops being justice for the Kirk family," Neiman, an attorney for Kirk's widow, Erika , told the court at the Oct. 23 hearing.
